description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of samples generated (x-axis) and the Micro F1 score in percent (y-axis) for four different methods: TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, Re-TACRED, and SemEval. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Samples Generated,” is on a linear scale with tick marks at K=16, K=32, and K=64, representing sample sizes of 16, 32, and 64, respectively. The y-axis, labeled “Micro F1 (%)”, ranges from 25 to 50, with major gridlines at intervals of 5 percentage points. The blue line with circular markers, representing TACRED, begins at approximately 24% at K=16, rises to about 33% at K=32, and reaches 44% at K=64. The orange line with triangular markers, for TACRED-Revisit, starts near 25% at K=16, increases to roughly 41% at K=32, and ends at about 44% at K=64. The green line with diamond markers, corresponding to Re-TACRED, begins at 36% at K=16, jumps to 46% at K=32, and plateaus slightly at approximately 50% at K=64. The red line with square markers, for SemEval, starts at 44% at K=16, climbs to 50% at K=32, and reaches 53% at K=64. All lines show a generally increasing trend as the number of generated samples increases, with Re-TACRED and SemEval achieving the highest performance across all sample sizes.
